name: Picornaviruses, Hepatitis A and E, Rhinovirus and Norovirus

reference.source: Paniker's Textbook of Medical Parasitology 8th Ed + Ananthanarayan and Paniker's Textbook of Microbiology (topic maps; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Hand foot mouth is Coxsackie A; chest grippe is B
A and E never chronic; E kills pregnancies
reference.pathophysiology: Motor neuron invasion ascends peripherally while enteroviral myocarditis scars conduction; HAV self limits as interferon clears, and norovirus VP1 shrugs sanitisers persisting on rails.
additionalDifferentials: Polio versus GBS by asymmetry and sensory sparing
Coxsackie A versus aphthae by hand foot lesions
HAV versus HEV by pregnancy course
additionalInvestigations: Stool isolation with AFP surveillance in floppy weakness
IgM anti HAV with LFTs in travel jaundice
Norovirus PCR with ward bleach protocol in outbreaks
